tagline: Along the shore of a lake that drowned its own highway.
intro: The byway leaves Topton on US 129 and runs north through Robbinsville to Deals Gap, by the Tennessee line, where it turns onto NC 28. From there it follows Cheoah Lake on the Little Tennessee and then the south shore of Fontana Lake, with the Great Smoky Mountains National Park across the water, and comes out at Almond.

Near Stecoah, large pipes run up the mountainsides. They carry the dams' overflow uphill to wait, and when the water runs low it comes back down to turn the turbines. The road by the lake was NC 288 until the lake came. Most of it went under, and the new road from Fontana to Almond was not finished until 1954.

moments.title: Robbinsville
moments.text: The Graham County seat's 1874 courthouse lost its floor two decades later, while the building was packed for a murder trial, and the town is now on its third, finished in 1942.

moments.title: Deals Gap
moments.text: The byway turns off US 129 just short of the state line, and the motorcyclists keep on into Tennessee for the Tail of the Dragon, said to hold 318 curves in 11 miles.

moments.title: Fontana Dam
moments.text: A side road crosses the 480-foot dam, as the Appalachian Trail does, and behind it the towns of Fontana, Bushnell, Forney and Judson lie under the lake.

practical: Tractor-trailers are prohibited on NC 28 along this stretch, and the state guidebook does not recommend it for recreational vehicles or buses.
